This is a classic cognitive bias called the *frequency illusion* (or Baader-Meinhof phenomenon). Your brain has a reticular activating system that filters out most sensory input. You saw him once, your brain logged it, and then it started actively looking for red jackets. It’s not a glitch in reality; it’s a glitch in your attention filter.

This one is also well-documented in neuroscience. Your eyes are constantly making micro-saccades (tiny, rapid movements). Your brain stitches together a stable image from these snapshots, but it doesn't process peripheral vision in high detail.
